subject: Post-call recap: lightweight masking strategy for request/response logs
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Moore <alicia.moore@nimbus-analytics.com>, Carlos Reyes <carlos.reyes@nimbus-analytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Nov 2025 15:12:00 -0500
Subject: Post-call recap: lightweight masking strategy for request/response logs

Thanks for the time earlier — quick recap and clear next steps from our side. High-level notes from the discovery call: 

- Scope: Nimbus wants to prevent PII from appearing in request/response logs (bodies + headers) while preserving the ability to correlate requests for debugging and analytics.
- Concern areas called out: user identifiers inside headers (X-User-Email), trace IDs used by upstream systems that also map to internal sessions, occasional sensitive payloads (SSN, payment tokens), and regulatory residency for audit copies.
- Retention ask: primary retention window ~90 days for sanitized logs; ability to keep raw debug captures for 7 days limited to an ops group under strict access controls.
- Compliance: need for demonstrable redaction approach for SOC2 evidence and a short POC to validate that redaction does not break observability.

Attachments: redaction-options-overview.pdf (proposal / pros & cons table).

Proposed next steps (we offered):
1) Redwood to propose two viable approaches for trace IDs/headers: a) deterministic one-way hash with per-customer salt (non-reversible) and b) prefix-preserve tokenization (keep first N chars). Provide tradeoffs for troubleshooting and analytics. -- owner: Sean (by 2025-11-30)
2) Provide a short POC checklist (data flows, sample sanitized logs, S3/Drive share + guidelines). -- owner: Monica
3) Nimbus to share SOC/security contact and a small sample (redacted) of typical request logs for feasibility testing. -- owner: Alicia

Please confirm the security contact and whether the 7-day raw debug window (ops-only) is acceptable as written. I can follow up with a short POC plan and an implementation feasibility note from engineering.

Thanks,
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redaction-options-overview.pdf (PDF)]

From: Alicia Moore <alicia.moore@nimbus-analytics.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Carlos Reyes <carlos.reyes@nimbus-analytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Nov 2025 10:05:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: lightweight masking strategy for request/response logs

Sean — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our security team that will determine the POC scope: 

- Trace IDs: we cannot remove trace IDs entirely because our incident pipeline uses them to stitch spans across services. We need options that prevent reconstruction of user identities while still allowing cross-system correlates. Deterministic hashing with a customer-scope salt sounds promising but we need an explanation of key rotation and how to prevent rainbow-table attacks.

- Retention: the 90-day sanitized retention is fine. The ops-only 7-day raw window is acceptable in principle, but the ops team needs a documented access process (justification + audit record).

- Sampling: we prefer a configurable sampling policy — e.g., 0.1% full-body captures + higher sampling for errors. Will want to ensure sampled captures are time-limited and marked in audit logs.

- Evidence: attach Nimbus security requirements (nimbus-security-reqs.xlsx). Please include a proposed mechanism for marking sampled records so they can be programmatically excluded from analytics and PII scans.

We can share a small synthetic sample of logs early next week. Our security contact is Carlos Reyes (cc'd).

Alicia Moore
Head of Platform Security, Nimbus Analytics
[Attachment: nimbus-security-reqs.xlsx (XLSX)]

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Moore <alicia.moore@nimbus-analytics.com>, Carlos Reyes <carlos.reyes@nimbus-analytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Nov 2025 09:20:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: lightweight masking strategy for request/response logs

Thanks Alicia — appreciate the specifics. Based on your constraints, we recommend two practical approaches with implementation notes and tradeoffs: 

Option A — Per-customer salted hash (recommended for privacy):
- Compute H = HMAC_SHA256(salt_customer, trace_id) and store truncated H (first 16 hex chars) in logs. Salt is stored in KMS; rotation is supported by maintaining salt versioning. Deterministic mapping preserves correlation across services but is non-reversible when salt is kept secret.
- Pros: strong privacy guarantees; works well for analytics joins.
- Cons: troubleshooting across systems requires everyone to use the same salt/version or a translation service.

Option B — Prefix-preserve tokenization:
- Keep the first 8 characters of trace_id and replace remainder with random characters (e.g., abcdef12-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx).
- Pros: lightweight, may preserve some human-readable clues for ops.
- Cons: weaker privacy guarantees; could leak entropy depending on upstream ID generation.

Additional controls:
- Body sampling: configurable sampling (default 0.1%) plus 100% captures on 5xx errors. Sampled captures are encrypted-at-rest with separate access controls and flagged in metadata.
- Header redaction: configurable ruleset (regex-based) to drop or mask common header names (Authorization, X-User-Email, Cookie). We can ship default safe list plus allow customer overrides.
- Access & audit: sampled/raw captures gated by role, justification entry, and retained audit trail for every access.

Proposed POC steps (attached poc-proposed-steps.md):
1) Provide synthetic logs from Nimbus. (Alicia)
2) Redwood runs an offline sanitization pass and returns sanitized samples and a short report (Monica)
3) Run an ingress-level redaction demo in our sandbox for 48 hours with your test workload (Monica & Neha)
4) Review results, tweak rules, and agree acceptance criteria for go/no-go.

Action items summary:
- Sean: deliver short one-page tradeoffs doc and sample config by 2025-11-30 (sent).
- Monica: schedule ingress demo and share POC checklist by 2025-12-03.
- Alicia/Carlos: share synthetic log samples and confirm ops access policy by 2025-12-02.

I attached the POC plan and will follow-up with calendar invites for the sandbox demo. Let me know if you prefer the prefix approach or salted hash as the starting point for the POC.

Best,
Sean
[Attachment: poc-proposed-steps.md]

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Moore <alicia.moore@nimbus-analytics.com>, Carlos Reyes <carlos.reyes@nimbus-analytics.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Dec 2025 09:03:00 -05:00
Subject: RE: Post-call recap: lightweight masking strategy for request/response logs

A quick engineering note to clarify how we intend to implement the POC and production options so your security team can evaluate technical fit.

On Sun, Nov 30, 2025 at 09:20 AM Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Alicia — appreciate the specifics. Based on your constraints, we recommend two practical approaches with implementation notes and tradeoffs:
>
> Option A — Per-customer salted hash (recommended for privacy): ...

Implementation clarifications (engineering perspective):
- Ingress-level redaction: our gateway supports a pluggable filter chain that can run regex redaction and HMAC transforms before any data is written to request/response logs. That means raw payloads never land in the standard logging path unless sampling rules explicitly trigger capture.
- Salt & key management: salts are stored in customer-scoped keys in KMS (we integrate with AWS KMS / GCP KMS). Salt rotation is implemented as key versioning; we can maintain old salt versions for re-hashing translations during a configured overlap window.
- Audit and storage separation: sampled captures and raw debug files are written to a separate bucket with an ACL that requires NDA and IAM gating. Access events are shipped to an immutable audit stream (retained 365 days).
- Debugging workflow: we can provide a lightweight translation utility to map salted hashes to transient debug tokens for authorized ops sessions (requires key unwrap via KMS and an access justification).
- Residency: we can ensure both sanitized logs and sampled raw captures remain in the US-east region for your account and apply bucket-level residency controls.

For the POC we need:
1) A small set (up to 200) of synthetic or redacted requests that represent the types of headers and bodies you see. Please avoid sharing real PII — synthetic/scrubbed is fine.
2) Confirmation of the ops group email list who will be allowed debug access.
3) NDA / access terms for the sandbox bucket (we can share a short form if needed).

I'll kick off the sandbox environment once we have those items. Sean — I'll coordinate with Neha to schedule the 48-hour demo and share the checklist. Alicia/Carlos — feel free to ping me directly if you want a deeper technical walk-through before the POC (I can demo the filter chain).

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Engineering Manager, Core Inference Services
Redwood Inference
